title: Pure-tensor evaluation of currying naturality
statement: Let (C,J) be a site, R a sheaf of commutative rings, K,Kprime,L,Lprime,M,Mprime complexes of R-module sheaves, f:Kprime -> K, g:Lprime -> L, h:M -> Mprime cochain maps, and n an integer. Let a and aprime be degree-n morphisms from Hom(K,Hom(L,M)) to Hom(Tot(K tensor L),M), and for the primed triple respectively, satisfying HomTensorCurryCondition [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise]. Let alpha be the iterated Hom map from f,g,h [def-pur-hom-complex], beta the Hom map from the total tensor map f tensor g and h [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every U, source section s, W -> U, i,j and x in Kprime^i(W), y in Lprime^j(W), the (i+j,i+j+n) projections of alpha^n then aprime and of a then beta^n have equal localized evaluations on the (i,j) inclusion of the canonical image of x tensor y in the sheaf total tensor. This asserts equality on a single pure tensor, not equality of projected morphisms.

proof.text: Apply the primed currying condition to alpha^n(s). The componentwise functoriality formula in homComplex_exists, applied first to the outer projection and then the inner projection, gives h^(i+j+n)(phi_i(f^i(x))_j(g^j(y))). Here phi is the original source iterated-Hom section.

For the other evaluation apply the Hom functor projection formula to beta. The identity HomologicalComplex.ι_mapBifunctorMap restricts its precomposition map to the termwise tensor f^i tensor g^j on the (i,j) summand. Naturality of the tensorator of sheafification and its counit shows the tensorObjIsoSheafification comparison is natural; combine this with naturality of the sheafification unit. Consequently the canonical image of x tensor y is sent to the canonical image of f^i(x) tensor g^j(y). The unprimed currying condition yields the same value as the previous step, proving the equality.
